title: CryptoBTB: A Secure Hierarchical BTB for Diverse Instruction Footprint Workloads
problem: Branch Target Buffer (BTB) timing attacks allow adversaries to infer victim BTB updates and mistrain branch predictors, bypassing privilege-level isolation and secure enclave protection; existing encrypted BTB schemes either have security weaknesses or encrypt the BTB index in-pipeline, exposing high latency.
method: CryptoBTB proposes a hierarchical exclusive BTB structure where the index encryption is decoupled from the BTB set index computation. The encryption step uses a low-latency scheme that obscures the set mapping without being on the critical prediction path; the hierarchical organization (L1 BTB + L2 BTB) avoids the collision-prone flat structure of prior work (HyBP), allowing the BTB capacity to be better utilized for workloads with large instruction footprints and reducing same-thread collisions.

title: Efficient Weight Mapping and Resource Scheduling on Crossbar-based Multi-core CIM Systems
problem: Multi-core crossbar-based CIM systems (eFlash-based SoCs) must optimize for both latency and resource utilization. Key compiler challenges include high parallel processing overhead, suboptimal resource utilization, and inefficient crossbar array assignment for CNNs, resulting in poor latency and low array utilization.
method: Proposes resource scheduling strategy based on stream data processing to reduce intra-core and inter-core communication latency. Develops weight mapping strategy to maximize crossbar array utilization for CNN deployment. Applies stream-based processing to schedule data flows and reduce handoffs between cores.

title: 8.7 A Dual VDD-Temperature Sensor Employing Sensor Fusion with 2.4°C, 9mV (±3σ) Inaccuracy in 65nm CMOS
problem: Heterogeneous 3D chiplet systems face acute thermal and power delivery challenges: thermal hotspots from high power density and workload-dependent supply voltage (VDD) gradients require fine-grained spatiotemporal monitoring via temperature and VDD sensors, but achieving high accuracy without external references is difficult.
method: Dual-sensor design combining temperature and VDD measurement via sensor fusion in 65nm CMOS; achieves 2.4°C and 9mV (±3σ) inaccuracy without external references, operating reliably despite VDD scaling and noise across different SoC domains.

title: GLOVA: Global and Local Variation-Aware Analog Circuit Design with Risk-Sensitive Reinforcement Learning
problem: Analog/mixed-signal circuit design faces significant performance degradation from process, voltage, and temperature (PVT) variations and manufacturing mismatches, requiring iterative manual revisions and extensive simulations to achieve commercial-grade reliability.
method: GLOVA uses risk-sensitive reinforcement learning with ensemble-based critic to optimize analog circuit sizing while accounting for PVT variations and random mismatches. The framework employs mu-sigma evaluation and simulation reordering to reduce verification costs, supporting corner simulation and Monte Carlo methods for industrial-level validation.

title: Towards Training Robustness Against Dynamic Errors in Quantum Machine Learning
problem: Quantum machine learning training assumes static error rates in QNNs, but quantum noise is dynamic across time and qubits, causing performance degradation even when aggregate error rates appear similar.
method: A novel noise-aware training strategy dynamically adjusts to standard and fatal error conditions during QNN optimization, incorporating low-complexity fatal-error detection to identify problematic error patterns and adapt training accordingly.

title: Computational Advantage in Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks: Myth or Reality?
problem: Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks (HQNNs) are proposed for enhanced computational performance, but it is unclear whether quantum layers provide genuine computational advantage over classical models when both scale to handle increasing problem complexity.
method: Comprehensive benchmarking of classical networks at increasing problem complexity identifies efficiency-optimal baselines. HQNNs (simulated on classical hardware) are systematically compared by measuring FLOP scaling and parameter growth rates as problem complexity increases (10 to 110 features), revealing architectural scaling efficiency differences.

title: 28.4 A 143dB-Dynamic-Range 119dB-CMRR Capacitance-to-Digital Converter for High-Resolution Floating-Target Displacement Sensing
problem: Capacitive displacement sensors for nanomechatronic systems are susceptible to high-frequency electric-field interference on electrically floating targets, requiring rejection of both low-frequency and high-frequency noise while maintaining high dynamic range (up to 500pF).
method: Phase-Domain-Delta-Sigma modulator (PD-ΔΣM) converts sensing capacitance to phase shift via lowpass RC front-end, then digitizes with high-resolution modulator. Inherent filtering in front-end/readout circuits provides dual-band noise rejection: 119dB CMRR near DC, 97dB around 100MHz, achieving 143dB dynamic range (35.2aF–500pF) without sub-ranging.

title: A 3x3.3mm Configurable Gamma Photon Spectrometer for Precision Radioguided Cancer Resection
problem: Radioguided surgery (RGS) for cancer removal requires gamma-sensing probes that can detect lesions at depth, differentiate lesion size/depth, and operate with high specificity; existing probes lack configurability, form-factor, and energy resolution.
method: A 180nm CMOS gamma spectrometer ASIC provides: (1) mm-scale pixelated design with single-gamma sensitivity, (2) per-pixel configurability for adaptive gain/threshold based on flux and PVT, (3) energy-resolving scheme with dynamic range to encode lesion depth via gamma energy profiles.

title: ByteFS: System Support for (CXL-based) Memory-Semantic Solid-State Drives
problem: Memory-semantic SSDs expose both byte-addressable (via PCIe/CXL load/store) and block interfaces simultaneously, but existing software systems are designed for either NVM on the processor memory bus or block-interface SSDs, and cannot efficiently exploit the unique dual-interface characteristics and distinct performance profiles of memory-semantic SSDs.
method: ByteFS is a file system designed specifically for CXL-based memory-semantic SSDs. It exploits the byte interface for metadata and small random accesses (latency-sensitive operations) while using the block interface for large sequential data transfers (throughput-sensitive operations), routing operations to the appropriate interface based on access pattern and size. ByteFS introduces new OS abstractions (allocation, caching, I/O path) that account for the asymmetric performance characteristics of the two interfaces and the persistent byte-addressable semantics provided by the device.

title: Piccolo: Large-Scale Graph Processing with Fine-Grained in-Memory Scatter-Gather
problem: Graph processing requires irregular fine-grained random memory accesses incompatible with DDR memory access granularity, leading to massive bandwidth waste and cache capacity waste; existing approaches using graph tiling (maximizing on-chip reuse) or PIM (placing arithmetic near memory) each have limitations when implemented with DDR standards, and combining them is difficult.
method: Piccolo implements non-arithmetic function-in-memory focused specifically on fine-grained random scatter-gather operations in off-chip memory, avoiding expensive arithmetic units inside DRAM. The accelerator's cache and miss-handling architecture (MHA) are redesigned to work compatibly with in-memory scatter-gather, enabling both graph tiling (on-chip data reuse) and in-memory operations simultaneously. The scatter-gather function-in-memory reduces off-chip traffic without requiring the expensive multi-operation support that makes traditional PIM impractical.

title: An Eye-Opening Arbiter PUF for Fingerprint Generation Using Auto-Error Detection for PVT-Robust Masking and Bit Stabilization Achieving a BER of 2e-8 in 28nm CMOS
problem: Physically unclonable functions (PUFs) for hardware identification and key generation must maintain constant fingerprint across voltage, temperature, and time variations while minimizing bit error rate (BER), but prior techniques either sacrifice speed/area for low BER via averaging/masking or rely on shared/off-chip error-correction hardware with security risks.
method: Arbiter-PUF design combining auto-error-detection circuitry with PVT-robust masking to stabilize bit readout across environmental variations, achieving BER of 2e-8 in 28nm CMOS without large error-correction overhead.

title: GauRast: Enhancing GPU Triangle Rasterizers to Accelerate 3D Gaussian Splatting
problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) requires significant computation, making real-time rendering infeasible on resource-constrained edge GPUs; prior acceleration via dedicated accelerators incurs high integration and hardware costs.
method: Enhances existing GPU rasterizer hardware (rather than building dedicated accelerator) to support 3DGS operations by recognizing algorithmic similarities with conventional graphics pipelines. Optimizes rasterizer datapath to handle Gaussian splatting primitive types and blending operations.

title: HetEC: Architectures for Heterogeneous Quantum Error Correction Codes
problem: Surface codes for quantum error correction scale quadratically in physical overhead with the number of correctable errors, making them resource-prohibitive at scale. Quantum LDPC (qLDPC) codes offer superior scaling but lack a clear path to universal logical computation on their own; no architecture jointly exploits both code families.
method: HetEC designs quantum computer architectures that combine surface codes and qLDPC codes in a heterogeneous manner. Surface code regions handle operations requiring local topological structure and magic state distillation for universal gate sets, while qLDPC code regions provide superior error-correction scaling. The architecture defines interfaces and protocols for logical qubit transfer and gate teleportation between code boundaries, enabling universal logical computation across the heterogeneous fabric.

title: A 3nm FinFET 2.2Gsearch/s 0.305fJ/b TCAM with Dynamically Gated Search Lines for Data-Center ASICs
problem: Ternary content-addressable memory (TCAM) for packet classification in data-center networks consumes excessive power due to parallel all-entry search, impacting operational efficiency and environmental footprint of network devices.
method: A 3nm FinFET TCAM design uses dynamically gated search-line (DGSL) architecture to selectively enable search operations, and asymmetric-split architecture (ASA) for bit-width-dependent power scaling, achieving 37.4% power savings and 46.6% peak-current reduction.

title: ChatLS: Multimodal Retrieval-Augmented Generation and Chain-of-Thought for Logic Synthesis Script Customization
problem: Logic synthesis script customization is manually intensive and design-specific; no automated method exists to adapt synthesis parameters to individual design characteristics.
method: ChatLS integrates multimodal RAG to retrieve relevant synthesis examples and design patterns, then uses chain-of-thought prompting to guide LLM reasoning over design features and synthesis constraints to generate customized TCL scripts.

title: The Unwritten Contract of Cloud-based Elastic Solid-State Drives
problem: Despite widespread cloud adoption, the performance characteristics and suitability of Elastic SSDs (ESSDs) as local SSD replacements remain uncharacterized, leaving cloud storage users uncertain about deployment decisions.
method: Characterizes two production ESSDs from AWS and Alibaba Cloud through comprehensive benchmarking, identifies counter-intuitive performance patterns, and derives design implications for cloud software optimization to exploit ESSD-specific characteristics.
